dateCheck: Wires read to 23:59 UTC, Monday 23 November 2026: every story here happened, or was first reported, on 23 November in at least one time zone. Left out because they happened on earlier days: the Shenzhen Xi–Trump–Putin summit (Thu 19 Nov) · the Coalition of the Willing summit in Berlin (Thu 19 Nov) · Democrats reaching 258 House seats (Sun 22 Nov) · the UK–EU reset deal (Fri 20 Nov) · the “El Chapo Isidro” arrest (Fri 20 Nov — Monday's toll + US drone help ARE in) · the COP31 collapse itself (Sun 22 Nov — Monday's reckoning IS in) · Liverpool 4–0 Man Utd · Alcaraz wins the ATP Finals · Verstappen wins the Las Vegas GP · Wembanyama's 50 (all Sun 22 Nov) · Hong Kong Election Committee vote (Sun 22 Nov) · the Sparta II drone hit (Sat 21 Nov) · BepiColombo's orbit insertion (Sat 21 Nov — ESA's “safe” statement Mon IS in) · the Merkury attack (Sun 22 Nov — Zelenskyy's confirmation Mon IS in) · the Indonesia factory fire outbreak (Sat 21 Nov — the death toll confirmed Mon IS in) · the NWSL final + Copa Sudamericana final (Sat 21 Nov) · the ICJ Myanmar genocide ruling (Thu 19 Nov) · Nvidia's CEO resignation (12 Nov) · the Anthropic IPO (19 Nov) · the Skubal deal agreed Sun evening (reported Mon) · the Larkin trade announced Sun night (Larkin's Montreal debut Mon IS in) · Likud–Yashar talks ended Sun (reported Mon).
pressTime: Wires read to 23:59 UTC, Monday 23 November 2026

stories.body: No deal after 49 hours of overtime, the longest COP ever and the first collapse since Copenhagen 2009. Guterres voices “profound frustration”, Gore calls it “outrageous” that a handful of petrostates hold a veto, chair Bowen cites “unbridgeable red lines”.
stories.headline: COP31 ends in failure — and the blame game begins

stories.body: Air traffic halted 07:00–21:00, 429 flights cancelled, 59,500 passengers grounded; trains and buses disrupted in a protest against the De Wever government's austerity plans.
stories.headline: Belgium stops for a national strike

stories.body: Around 60 banks cut off from SWIFT, 70+ shadow-fleet ships listed, the Russian flag banned at EU sports events, and a visa ban on former combatants, announced by von der Leyen.
stories.headline: EU unveils its 22nd sanctions package

stories.body: Zelenskyy confirms on Monday: seven Ukrainian sea drones sank the corvette Merkury at Benghazi, destroyed a Ka-27 helicopter and hit the cargo ship MV Angara. The attack was Sunday; the confirmation is Monday.
stories.headline: Ukraine sinks Russian warship 2,400 km from the front

stories.body: The death toll from the Russian strike on an apartment block in Dymer, Kyiv region, rises to at least 11 in Monday's update; 14 people were still listed missing on Sunday.
stories.headline: Dymer strike toll reaches at least 11

stories.body: Debris found at all three crash sites in Poland came from Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles, prosecutors say, revising the account given over the weekend.
stories.headline: Missile debris in Poland was Russian, prosecutors say

stories.body: ESA says the probe is stable after a software glitch cut its braking burn to 77% of the planned change in velocity. Orbiter separation stays on track for 9 December.
stories.headline: BepiColombo is safe in Mercury orbit

stories.body: Final polls before Sunday's election — and before the five-day blackout — put the PP and Vox together above 176 seats in the 350-seat house, despite Socialist gains. Monday is the last day polls may be published.
stories.headline: Spain's right on course for a majority

stories.body: A second group of children from Gaza arrives in Britain for NHS treatment, the government confirms on Monday morning.
stories.headline: Second wave of Gaza children reaches the UK

stories.body: The Commission says its EU Academy learning platform leaked users' names and email addresses in an AI-assisted cyber campaign, and takes the site offline. The scale is still under investigation.
stories.headline: EU confirms a data breach after cyberattack

stories.body: Iran's army says it downed an American “Lucas” drone over the Persian Gulf, east of Hormuz, on Monday evening. The claim, carried by Tasnim, is one side's account.
stories.headline: Iran says it shot down a US drone

stories.body: Two supertankers are reported hit by mines in the Strait of Hormuz in an incident on Sunday, reported by the IRGC navy early on Monday. Shipping through the strait is on edge.
stories.headline: Two supertankers hit mines in Hormuz

stories.body: Rolling power cuts bite across Iran as fuel runs short at power plants. Pezeshkian is filmed working by a single lamp and urges the public to save electricity; the cuts were announced Saturday and began Sunday.
stories.headline: Iran's lights go out — president films his dark office

stories.body: Bahrain demands full compensation from Iran and urges the UN Security Council to act, in a statement issued just after midnight GMT.
stories.headline: Bahrain demands Iran pay in full

stories.body: Likud and Yashar conclude a four-hour round of coalition talks with no agreement on who leads a unity government or whether Ben-Gvir sits in it. Eisenkot has until 6 December to form a government; the talks ended Sunday, reported Monday.
stories.headline: Netanyahu–Eisenkot unity talks end without a deal

stories.body: The US president says strikes on Iran could resume after the new year if no deal is reached, keeping the threat on the table as the naval blockade holds.
stories.headline: Trump: Iran strikes could resume in the new year

stories.body: Iran's Foreign Ministry says Tehran will use “all means” against the US naval blockade, as the standoff over shipping and sanctions deepens.
stories.headline: Iran vows “all means” against the blockade

stories.body: The Kospi closes down 3.3%, its lowest since 13 January, and the Hang Seng touches a 19-month low. Taiwan rebounds 2.2% under a short-sale ban; Tokyo is shut for a holiday; Seoul readies a stabilisation fund.
stories.headline: Asian markets slide again

stories.body: The death toll from Saturday's factory fire is confirmed at 24 on Monday, with around 30 people still missing, as rescuers keep searching the wreckage.
stories.headline: Indonesia factory fire: 24 dead, ~30 missing

stories.body: New Zealand bat out 120 overs at 239/5 to save the Test. India declared on 720/9 — a record Test total in New Zealand — with Rahul on 136, Pant 128 and Nicholls unbeaten on 175.
stories.headline: India–NZ Test drawn after a record stand

stories.body: Modi announces a 240-billion-rupee (€1.4bn) package for Nepal's reconstruction after August's deadly glacier flood, standing beside PM Shah in New Delhi on his first bilateral trip abroad.
stories.headline: India pledges €1.4bn to rebuild Nepal

stories.body: Dhaka says it will arrest and jail former prime minister Sheikh Hasina if she comes back to Bangladesh, as her trial in absentia continues.
stories.headline: Bangladesh: Hasina will be jailed if she returns

stories.body: Treasury Secretary Bessent says Washington is pressing Nvidia over sales of its chips to China's government, as the AI export fight spills into the open.
stories.headline: US presses Nvidia over China chip sales

stories.body: All 311 passengers are rescued after a fast craft catches fire in the Philippines, in one of the day's quieter pieces of good news.
stories.headline: 311 rescued from burning fast craft

stories.body: Beijing sets 2030 targets for elderly care and childcare, the latest step in its push to cushion a shrinking, ageing population.
stories.headline: China sets 2030 care targets

stories.body: Nvidia's board reinstates Jensen Huang as chief executive 11 days after his resignation. Shares jump 31.5% — the best day since 2003 — adding $952bn in value; the S&P gains 4.8%, the Nasdaq 6.5%, the Dow 1,448 points.
stories.headline: Huang is back — Nvidia soars 31.5%

stories.body: Bitcoin jumps from about $61,200 to about $63,900 on the Nvidia news, and gold adds $50 to $3,666 as risk appetite returns.
stories.headline: Bitcoin and gold ride the Nvidia wave

stories.body: Two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal agrees a nine-year, $450m deal with the Mets — the largest ever for a pitcher, topping Yamamoto's $325m. Agreed Sunday evening, reported Monday.
stories.headline: Skubal signs a record $450m Mets deal

stories.body: Ex-Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin skates with the Canadiens on Monday morning after Sunday night's blockbuster trade — Dach, Montembeault, Hage and two first-round picks go the other way — and debuts against the Kings tonight.
stories.headline: Larkin lands in Montreal

stories.body: The death toll from the operation that captured cartel boss “El Chapo Isidro” is updated to 20 — four soldiers and 16 cartel members — and US help with a drone is confirmed. The capture itself was Friday night.
stories.headline: “El Chapo Isidro” capture: toll now 20

stories.body: Doctors rule out surgery for now after an endoscopy removed fibrous material from the former president's stomach; pneumonia is diagnosed during his stay. He remains in intensive care in Brasília with no discharge date.
stories.headline: Bolsonaro stays in ICU; surgery ruled out

stories.body: Rookie kicker Drew Stevens hits a 26-yard field goal with no time left as Washington rallies past Cincinnati 22-20 on Monday Night Football — after the stadium lights briefly went out in the third quarter.
stories.headline: Commanders stun Bengals 22-20 on last-second kick

stories.body: Tyler Herro scores 32 as Milwaukee beats Toronto 116-111 to end a 13-game losing streak — the best of ten games on Monday night. SGA's 38 cannot save the Thunder in Indiana; Portland ends the Sixers' five-game run; the Spurs win their 13th straight.
stories.headline: Bucks snap 13-game skid, 116-111

stories.body: Anthropic shares ease to about $86.47 as money floods back into Nvidia. The AI lab went public on 19 November at $83.
stories.headline: Anthropic slips as Nvidia rallies

stories.body: Nairobi and Kinshasa restore ambassador-level relations, announced on Monday after the two presidents agreed the step at Sunday's summit in Oyo.
stories.headline: Kenya and DR Congo restore full ties

stories.body: At least 64 people are killed in weekend attacks in Nigeria's Niger State, blamed on Fulani groups, in reports carried on Monday.
stories.headline: 64 killed in weekend attacks in Niger State

stories.body: Opposition leader Brian Mundubile is committed to the High Court in Lusaka to face treason charges, in a case that will test Zambia's courts.
stories.headline: Zambia opposition leader faces treason trial

stories.body: At least 24 civilians are killed in an attack in South Sudan's Tonj East county on Saturday night into Sunday, reported on Monday.
stories.headline: At least 24 civilians killed in Tonj East

stories.body: Heavy fighting in DR Congo's Ituri province traps teams responding to the Ebola outbreak, the WHO says on Monday evening.
stories.headline: Fighting in Ituri traps Ebola responders

stories.body: The Countdown host who championed AC/DC, Kylie Minogue and ABBA — and brought Australian music to the world — dies aged 83. Tributes pour in from across the industry.
stories.headline: Molly Meldrum dies aged 83

stories.body: Foreign Minister Penny Wong will use a Senate speech to defend Australia's alliance with the United States and the AUKUS pact, as the debate over both sharpens.
stories.headline: Wong to defend the US alliance in the Senate

stories.body: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese meets Singapore's Prime Minister Lawrence Wong in Canberra for talks on trade, defence and the region.
stories.headline: Albanese meets Singapore's Wong in Canberra

stories.body: Albanese stands by climate minister Chris Bowen after the COP31 collapse, as the opposition demands Bowen's resignation over the failed summit he chaired.
stories.headline: Albanese stands by Bowen after COP31

stories.body: The sweeping Defence Bill — secret security zones, up to seven years' jail for entering one — passes its final hurdle as the House agrees to Senate amendments on Monday evening. Scholars call it “lazy and irresponsible”.
stories.headline: Defence Bill clears parliament

stories.body: African energy exporters gained an extra $21.6bn during the war on Iran, a CREA report says on Monday, with Nigeria alone up $7.5bn on higher prices and volumes.
stories.headline: African exporters gained $21.6bn from the Iran war

stories.body: The UN mission in Libya calls for an independent investigation into the attacks on Benghazi port — the same port where Ukraine says it sank the Merkury.
stories.headline: UN mission in Libya wants a probe

timeline.text: Bahrain demands Iran pay in full
IRGC: tankers hit mines in Hormuz
Belgium airspace shuts for the strike
Iran: US drone downed, it claims
Wires close — the full day is in

title: THE WORLD IN ONE DAY
